  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not
listed on the agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be
taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each
speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Time may be surrendered by deferring (1) one minute to another speaker,
not to exceed a total of (8) eight minutes. The speaker wishing to defer time must be present when the item is
heard. In order to be recognized and present an item, each speaker must complete and submit to the Recording
Secretary a Request to Speak form prior to the beginning of the item being announced by the Chair (forms are
available at the entrance to the meeting room). Speakers are taken in the order slips are submitted.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting
where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public
discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning
decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of
the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is
desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may
indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to
adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission
following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting

Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall
follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are
on file in the City Clerk Department, Malibu City Hall, 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California and are
available for public inspection during regular office hours which are 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday through
Thursday, and 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Friday. Written materials distributed to the Commission within 72 hours
of the Commission meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution (Government Code
Section 54957.5(b)(2). Copies of staff reports and written materials may be purchased for $0.10 per page.
Pursuant to State law, this agenda was posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the
deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance

[28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was

ITEM 4  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Meeting Schedule
  Recommended action: 1) Determine the meeting day and time for
  Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Regular Meetings; and 2)
  Request staff bring back a resolution to adopt the regular meeting date and
  time.

  Deputy City Manager Rojas presented the staff report and stated the options
  available to the commission for the proposed regular meeting schedule is
  the first or third Thursday of each month or the third Wednesday of each
  month. He explained the scheduling of this current meeting is a result of
  room and staff availability. He asked Deputy City Clerk Muñoz for
  confirmation there is room availability for the remainder of the calendar
  year.

  In response to the question, Deputy City Clerk Muñoz confirmed that the
  room is available for the remainder of the year, and that the proposed days
  provided in the staff report do not interrupt or overlap with other
  programming, like the senior luncheon or other commission meetings.

  Chair Shenkmen opened the floor to public comment.
   Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Meeting Minutes
  September 11, 2025
  Page 3 of 7
  ______________________

  Candace Bowen-Ferguson, Vice President of Point Dume Club Residence
  Association, supported adoption of a standing, predictable meeting date and
  time to facilitate public participation and outreach (including residents’
  email notifications).

  Dru Ann Jacobson and Terry Surgis addressed preferred days/times and
  encouraged a regular schedule that accommodates residents.

  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Shenkman returned the
  matter to the table for discussion.

  Commissioner Grisanti provided his availability. Commissioner Sampson
  apologized for his tardiness and stated he is here to best serve the
  commission and also provided his availability.

  Chair Shenkman stated that Government Code section 54954 requires the
  commission to set a regular meeting, including place and time. He also
  stated that City Council directed this body to have one meeting a month for
  the remainder of the calendar year.

  Vice Chair Sampson asked if the November meeting would conflict with
  the Thanksgiving holiday. Deputy City Clerk Muñoz clarified that the
  selected schedule is not interrupted by any of the upcoming holidays.

  Chair Shenkman stated the Brown Act requires that regular meeting
  agendas be posted at least 72 hours in advance, setting Monday as the
  posting day.

  He stated Commissioners discussed ensuring that regular meetings are not
  cancelled due solely to the unavailability of the Chair or Vice Chair and that
  any necessary cancellations will be noticed reasonably.

MOTION  Chair Shenkman moved, and Commissioner Grisanti seconded, to establish
  the Commission’s regular meetings on the third Thursday of each month at
  1:30 p.m. at Malibu City Hall – Council Chambers. The question was called,
  and the motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Chair Shenkman moved, and Commissioner Grisanti seconded, a motion
  for meetings to not be cancelled absent of the vice chair or chair.

  B.  Process for Annual Formula Rent Increase
  Recommended action: Receive and file.

  Deputy City Manager Rojas presented the staff report. He stated park
  owners must first submit an annual registration form to the city. He stated
  the City’s annual notice to park owners regarding the maximum permitted
   Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Meeting Minutes
  September 11, 2025
  Page 4 of 7
  ______________________
rent increase was sent out in December 2024 informing them a 2.2%
increase was permitted based on CPI.

Chair Shenkmen opened the floor to public comment.

Dru Ann Jacobson asked whether rent could be increased beyond the
noticed percentage; staff/Commission clarified the notice reflects the
maximum allowed.

Terry Surgis requested a copy of the City’s notice.

Candace Bowen-Ferguson referenced residents’ records and asked about
ensuring consistency year to year.

As there were no other speakers present, Chair Shenkman returned the
matter to the table for discussion.

Commissioner Grisanti stated the ordinance’s caped the increase at 5%. He
stated that years ago when the increase was 7% it was only able to be 5%.

Chair Shenkman confirmed the ceiling of the increase was 5%; unless it
below 2% or above 5%.

Interim City Attorney Rusin clarified the notice simply defines the
maximum allowed increase, not a required one. Park owners remain
responsible for staying within the legal ceiling.

Chair Shenkman questioned whether the correct CPI series had been used,
noting the ordinance references the obsolete Los Angeles–Riverside–
Orange County index and that staff notices have referenced Los Angeles–
Long Beach–Anaheim. He requested verification that the current Los
Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim CPI is appropriate. He noted potential
variance between CPI series, he stated this year the Los Angeles–Long
Beach–Anaheim’s was 3.2% as noted in the notice and the CPI increase for
Riverside, San Bernardino, Ontario was 1.10% .

Chair Shenkman stated the City has the authority to select any CPI index,
they do not arbitrarily have to use the Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim
index.

Deputy City Manager Rojas responded the Los Angeles–Long Beach–
Anaheim index is the closest corresponding CPI published by the Bureau of
Labor Statistics.

Vice Chair Sampson stated park owners are operating on the honor system
to increase the rent the amount the City states is allowed. He expressed
interest in ensuring all the increases are valid and legitimate.

CONSENSUS The Commission through consensus agreed they would like copies of the
  Rent increase reports.

  C.  Review of Existing Applications for Mobile Home Space Adjustment
  Recommended action: Receive and file.

  Deputy City Manager Rojas stated there are three existing application forms
  that are available to the public on the Ctiy website. He explained that there
  has not been much utilization of those applications based on existing
  records. Staff does make them available consistent with the requirements of
  the ordinance.

  Commissioner Grisanti stated asked if the application for mobilehome rent
  adjustment are being submitted and completed.

  Deputy City Manager Rojas confirmed they are being submitted and
  completed. He explained while the commission went dark staff defaulted to
  completing the review of the applications.

  Chair Shenkman and Vice Chair Sampson asked why staff was performing
  the review of the applications.

  Commissioner Grisanti explained that the commission initially heard
  multiple applications, but park owners realized their requests to increase
  rent beyond the allowed ceiling were consistently being denied. As a result,
  the commission eventually had no work to do. Although commissioners
  continued to file Form 700s, they eventually resigned. The commission then
  became inactive for 17 years.

  During this period, tenants and park owners developed a cooperative
  relationship, characterized by mutual agreement, a lack of tension, and
  general collaboration between the two parties.

  Chair Shenkmen opened the floor to public comment.

  Dru Ann Jacobson agreed with the Commissioner Grisanti, the park owners
  and tenants had an amicable relationship.

  Terry Surgis, stated residence of the park at one point in time were
  interested in purchasing the land. She stated challenges due to not all tenants
  having desire to purchase the land.

  Candace Bowen-Ferguson explained she would like some direction on how
  to navigate the process and what can be done to assist the mobilehome park
  residents.
   Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission Meeting Minutes
  September 11, 2025
  Page 6 of 7
  ______________________
  As there were no other speakers present, Chair Shenkman returned the
  matter to the table for discussion.

  Chair Shenkman stated that, he finds the process challenging for tenants to
  navigate and the process is extremely outdated. He noted the forms appear
  to be from the early 90s. He stated as this matter may fall outside the scope
  of the current agenda item, he would like to place it on the agenda for the
  next meeting. He explained a sample updated form has been circulated to
  staff and requested that adoption of that form be considered at the next
  meeting, subject to review and input from the other commissioners.

  Chair Shenkman further expressed concern regarding a possible due process
  issue in the current application process. He explained that if a resident
  submits an application—whether using the simplified form or the more
  complex version historically used by the City. He explained that if staff
  deems it incomplete, the applicant may have to dispute that assessment. In
  such cases, he suggested there should be a mechanism for the disagreement
  to be brought before the Commission for a determination on completeness,
  ensuring a process consistent with due process requirements. He also stated
  the status and implications of Assembly Bill 768. He noted that the bill,
  which could eliminate rent control for 30–40% of Malibu’s mobile homes,
  passed the Assembly Housing Committee by a 7–2 vote but was pulled
  before being heard by the Judiciary Committee. He emphasized that the bill
  remains active and that there is significant legislative support, citing
  concerns that rent control on subleased mobile homes reduces overall
  housing supply.

  Commsioner Grisanti and Vice Chair agreed that form be brought back at
  another meeting.

  In response to Ms. Surgis public comment, Commissioner Grisanti stated a
  notice must be sent to tenants first for the opportunity to purchase the land.
  He indicated a letter should be sent yearly to the park owners expressing
  this interest.

  Vice Chair Sampson responded that he did not believe such a provision
  existed in the ordinance.

  Chair Shenkman suggested the formation of an Ad Hoc subcommittee of
  the Commission. The subcommittee would be tasked with drafting proposed
  amendments to the Malibu Mobile Home Rent Stabilization Ordinance. He
  proposed that the Commission review and discuss those recommendations
  at its November meeting, and, if supported, forward them to the City
  Council for consideration, potentially at a January Council meeting.

MOTION  Chair Shenkman moved, and Vice Chair Sampson seconded, a motion to
  form an Ad Hoc Subcommittee composed of Chair Shenkman and Vice

  ______________________
  Chair Sampson would be tasked with drafting proposed amendments to the
  Malibu Mobile Home Rent Stabilization Ordinance. The motion carried
  unanimously.

ITEM 5  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC
  AND COMMISSIONERS

  Chair Shenkman opened the floor to public comment. There were no

MOTION  At 2:39 p.m., Chair Shenkman moved, and Vice Chair Sampson seconded

Subject:  Adoption of a Resolution to Establish a Schedule for Regular
  Commission Meetings

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Adopt Resolution No. MPRSC 25-01, a resolution of the
Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission (Commission) of the City of Malibu
establishing the start time and place of regular meetings and superseding and replacing
all previous resolutions setting the start time and place of regular meetings.

DISCUSSION:  The Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission met on
September 11, 2025, to discuss setting a time, place, and day for which regular meetings
are to occur.

The Commission determined regular meetings of the Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization
Commission shall be held at Malibu City Hall - 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu,
California, 90265 at the hour of 1:30 p.m., on the third Thursday of each month; or, if any
such day is on a holiday, the meeting shall be re-scheduled to the next succeeding
business day which is not a holiday.

Since the next meeting day is typically a Friday, rescheduled regular meetings may be
adjourned to a future date based on Commissioner, Staff, and room availability.

ATTACHMENTS: Resolution No. MPRSC 25-01

   RESOLUTION NO. MPRSC 25-01

  A RESOLUTION OF THE MOBILEHOME PARK RENT STABILIZATION
  COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF MALIBU ESTABLISHING THE START
  TIME AND PLACE OF REGULAR MEETINGS AND SUPERSEDING AND
  REPLACING ALL PREVIOUS RESOLUTIONS SETTING THE START TIME
  AND PLACE OF REGULAR MEETINGS

The Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission of the City of Malibu does hereby find,
order, and resolve as follows:

SECTION 1. Regular meetings of the Mobilehome Park Rent Stabilization Commission shall be
held at Malibu City Hall - 23825 Stuart Ranch Road, Malibu, California, 90265 at the hour of 1:30
p.m., on the third Thursday of each month, or, if any such day is on a holiday, then the meeting
scheduled on such day shall be held on the next succeeding day which is not a holiday.

SECTION 2. Adoption of this resolution supersedes and replaces all previous resolutions
establishing time and place for regular meetings.

SECTION 3. This Resolution shall become effective immediately upon its passage and adoption.

PASSED, APPROVED, and ADOPTED this 16th day of October 2025.

  KEVIN SHENKMAN, Chair
